focus: Find out where you actually stand before optimising anything.
items: Take one timed 45-min DSA mock cold, and write down what broke
Work the Hashing, Two Pointers and Sliding Window patterns end to end
Read Bias–variance, Regularisation and Gradient descent; be able to draw each
Write your 2-minute intro and three STAR stories
Math for ML: Bayes with a 1%-prevalence test, the CLT by averaging dice, a paired t-test and an A/B sample size by hand (math1, math4, math6, math7)
Behavioural foundations: learn how rounds are scored, build an 8–12 story bank with a stories × themes matrix, then record and score your 2-minute intro (beh1, beh2, beh3)
DSA patterns first: how to approach any problem, reading complexity off the constraints, then prefix sums and hashing with their templates (al1, al2, al3, al4)

focus: The theory that every AI-engineer loop still asks about.
items: Binary search (including on the answer) and Stacks — 12 problems
Metrics, thresholds, ROC vs PR — play with the threshold visual until it is obvious
Trees, random forests, gradient boosting — be able to say why GBDT wins on tabular
Linear algebra and calculus for ML: eigenvectors of a 2×2 and an SVD by hand, the chain rule through a 2-layer net, cross-entropy versus KL (math9, math10, math12)
Python cold: names and mutability, data-structure costs, closures and decorators, generators, the GIL and asyncio, and the gotchas list (py1, py2, py3, py4, py5, py9, py15)
Beyond the core models: an SVM's margin, dual and kernels by hand, confounding and uplift with a Qini curve, and Kaplan–Meier on a censored table (ml18, ml17, ml19)

focus: Backprop, normalisation, optimisers — enough to debug a training run out loud.
items: Optimisers and the memory arithmetic for a 7B model
First LLD: LRU cache and the rate limiter, written out by hand
PyTorch in practice: strides and views, autograd and in-place errors, a correct training loop, then find the eight planted bugs in the 80-line script (pt1, pt3, pt6, pt9)
GPU arithmetic: the roofline and arithmetic intensity, transformer FLOPs and bytes per token, and FP32-to-FP4 formats, worked for a 7B model (gpu1, gpu2, gpu3, gpu4)
Beyond images and labels: one GCN layer and over-smoothing by hand on a 4-node graph, then InfoNCE at four temperatures and why BYOL and DINO don't collapse (dl12, dl13)

focus: Attention from scratch — the highest-yield week for an AI-engineer loop.
items: Implement single-head attention in NumPy without looking anything up
Tokenisation, attention, transformer block, positional encodings
KV cache, MQA/GQA, and the KV memory formula
Scale fundamentals before design week: back-of-envelope estimation, caching, replication, sharding and consistency/CAP, each with one number you can say out loud (sc1, sc3, sc6, sc7, sc9)
Pre-transformer NLP: a TF-IDF + naive Bayes baseline with its cost case against an LLM, word2vec negative sampling by hand, and Viterbi for NER (ml20, ml21, ml22)

ML coding for modern models, timed: speculative decoding's rejection rule, a top-k MoE router, the DPO loss, int8 quantisation, CLIP's InfoNCE loss, word2vec, a tiny ViT with loop-free patchify, and an LSTM with hand-written BPTT and a gradient check (mc24–mc32)

focus: RAG, embeddings and fine-tuning as engineering, not demos.
items: RAG end to end: chunking, hybrid retrieval, reranking, evaluation
Embeddings, vector search, HNSW vs IVF-PQ, recall@k
LoRA/QLoRA and quantisation — both memory calculations
Evals by hand: a 95% interval on 78% from 200 cases, a judge swap test with kappa before and after, recall@5 and nDCG@5 for one query, and a paired bootstrap on two prompts (ev2, ev4, ev6, ev7)
Multimodal and reasoning: ViT and CLIP, how a VLM is wired, test-time compute and GRPO/RLVR — be able to draw each pipeline (mm1, mm2, mm3, rs1, rs2, rs4)
AI engineering basics: anatomy of a production LLM app, structured output that survives parsing, and prompt/context engineering (ae1, ae4, ae6)

The 2026 LLM questions by hand: KV cache versus a Mamba state at 4K and 128K, the KV bill and prefill FLOPs at 128K and 1M, RoPE scaling per frequency with YaRN's ramp, and the DPO loss and gradient weights on three preference pairs (lm21, lm22, lm23)

focus: Two full designs out loud, with numbers.
items: LLM serving platform and enterprise RAG — whiteboard both, timed
Recommendations and fraud detection — the classic ML-systems pair
Machine coding: vector index and the resilient LLM client
Databases: write joins, NULL traps and window functions live, read one EXPLAIN ANALYZE plan, and trace MVCC for two transactions (db3, db4, db7, db9)

Agents by hand: 0.95^10 and when a workflow beats an agent, a 3-tool ReAct episode as message JSON with token counts, cache savings over a 20-step run, a lethal-trifecta threat model with taint policies, and the 100k-tasks/day cost model under two routing policies (ag1, ag2, ag5, ag10, ag13)
Search & recsys: the funnel and latency budget, two-tower retrieval, learning to rank and ranking metrics (rec1, rec4, rec7, rec8), then whiteboard a feed design with numbers

Data engineering for ML: size a Parquet layout and a skewed Spark join, trace an Iceberg commit and a watermark, and whiteboard a CDC-to-training-shards pipeline with point-in-time joins and a monthly bill (de2, de4, de6, de9, de12, de13)
Classic and infra designs, timed: URL shortener, chat and news feed, then a message queue and a key-value store as building blocks (cd1, cd2, cd3, in1, in2)
Networking for design rounds: what happens when you type a URL, TCP, HTTP semantics, TLS and load balancers (net2, net4, net7, net9, net10)

Agents across boundaries: an A2A task through all its states with idempotent retries, the same refund agent in a graph framework, a conversation SDK and a hand-written loop, and a browser agent's token bill and recovery policy (ag15, ag16, ag17)

AI design additions, timed: a text-to-SQL agent's schema-linking recall and $10k-scan guard, a voice turn's per-stage budget and barge-in states, GPU-seconds per image with Erlang C, IVF-PQ memory for 1B vectors, filtered-HNSW collapse at 1%, and cost per usable label (hd22, hd23, hd24, hd25, hd26, hd27)

More classic designs and machine coding, timed: an order-matching engine, a flash sale, a leaderboard, live comments and a unique-ID generator (cd15–cd18, in14); then code an agent tool loop, a streaming JSON parser, an LFU cache and an in-memory file system in 45 minutes each (ld21, ld22, ld26, ld28)

focus: Cost, latency, evaluation, safety — the senior signal.
items: Inference optimisation: batching, speculative decoding, prefix caching
Evaluation stacks, LLM-as-judge and its biases, regression suites
Cost modelling and the routing/caching levers
Prompt injection, guardrails, and the agent failure taxonomy

Docker and Kubernetes: trace kubectl apply to a running pod, requests and limits to QoS and CPU-throttling maths, the HPA formula on a metric series, and GPU scheduling with gang admission and queue-depth autoscaling (k8s6, k8s10, k8s11, k8s14)

Evals in production: users needed to detect a 2-point online win, red-team per-goal success and severity, MinHash dedup and decontamination, and a CI regression gate plus an EWMA drift alert (ev8, ev9, ev11, ev12)

Auth & identity: recompute a JWT signature and a PKCE challenge by hand, answer 'can Alice edit doc 42?' with RBAC and ReBAC, fix an IDOR with row-level security, and design auth for a B2B SaaS with an AI assistant — users, services, tenants and agents (au4, au5, au8, au9, au12)

Cloud fundamentals: evaluate an IAM request with an allow and an explicit deny, plan and price a three-zone VPC, size DynamoDB capacity for a real workload, compute RTO and RPO for a DR plan, and cost a small web app and a GPU fine-tuning run (cl2, cl3, cl7, cl10, cl12, cl14)

PyTorch at scale: the activation-memory formula and an OOM fix, DDP buckets versus FSDP2 for a 7B model, a profiler trace with the syncs removed, and exporting and quantising a model for serving (pt7, pt11, pt12, pt13)

AI safety for senior loops: the four risk areas, what the alignment-faking and scheming papers did and did not show, your company's frontier framework with its version and date, and a timed ship-or-hold answer with numbers (sf1, sf4, sf8, sf12)

Product & metrics sense: pick a north star, guardrails and a counter-metric for one feature, decompose a 5% drop through a metric tree, read a scorecard against a minimum worthwhile effect and a non-inferiority margin, and size an AI feature's value per query against its cost (ps2, ps4, ps7, ps8)
GPU and inference performance: FlashAttention, ZeRO/FSDP memory, modelling LLM inference latency and throughput, and choosing hardware by cost (gpu7, gpu9, gpu10, gpu12)
Operating systems for senior loops: processes vs threads, synchronization and deadlock, virtual memory, and namespaces/cgroups under a container (os2, os4, os6, os8, os13)

AI engineering in production by hand: a semantic-cache threshold sweep priced in dollars, a TTFT budget before and after parallelising, self-host versus API break-even with utilisation, an on-device tokens-per-second ceiling, and a threat model for one feature with the EchoLeak chain (ae9, ae10, ae11, ae12, ae13)

Reasoning RL in practice: walk the R1 pipeline with its settings and $294K bill, compute Kimi's length reward and DAPO's overlong penalty by hand, design a hint-insertion faithfulness test, and harden a code verifier against exits, overrides and special-casing (rs9, rs10, rs11)

focus: Full loops under time pressure; fix only what the mocks expose.
items: Three full mock loops: DSA, ML depth, system design
Re-solve every problem you marked for review
Flashcard the whole question bank to 90%+ known
Prepare questions for them, and rehearse your project deep-dive

Behavioural mock: conflict, failure and influence questions with follow-ups, re-angled to your target company’s published values; then script your salary-expectations answer, BATNA and counter (beh4–beh10)

Timed product cases with a partner: two of the five ps12 cases in 40 minutes each (one diagnosis, one AI-feature launch bar), then the sixth case alone; note every skipped check and missed trap (ps1, ps12)
Software-engineering depth: API design, CI/CD and safe rollouts, observability, and a design doc you could defend (swe7, swe9, swe14, swe15)
